checks.description: S3 bucket ACL must not be set to public-read. The public-read canned ACL grants read access to all users including unauthenticated users, exposing bucket contents to the public internet.
checks.impact: Objects in the bucket are readable by any unauthenticated user on the internet, leading to data disclosure or exfiltration of sensitive content
checks.resolution: Set the acl attribute to private (the default), or remove the aws_s3_bucket_acl resource if not needed. Use bucket policies with explicit IAM principal restrictions instead of canned public ACLs.
checks.errorMessage: S3 bucket ACL is set to public-read, which exposes all objects to unauthenticated public access on the internet

checks.description: S3 bucket ACL must not be set to public-read-write. The public-read-write canned ACL grants read and write access to all users including unauthenticated users, allowing anyone to upload, modify, or delete objects.
checks.impact: Any unauthenticated user on the internet can read, write, or delete objects in the bucket, enabling data exfiltration, ransomware staging, content replacement, or abuse for malware hosting
checks.resolution: Set the acl attribute to private (the default). The public-read-write ACL must never be used in any environment. Use bucket policies with explicit deny rules and least-privilege IAM principals instead.
checks.errorMessage: S3 bucket ACL is set to public-read-write, which grants unrestricted read and write access to all internet users including unauthenticated users

checks.description: S3 bucket ACL must not be set to authenticated-read. The authenticated-read canned ACL grants read access to all authenticated AWS accounts — not just accounts in your organization, but any of the hundreds of millions of AWS accounts worldwide.
checks.impact: Any authenticated AWS user globally can read bucket contents, representing a broad and poorly scoped exposure that bypasses organizational access boundaries
checks.resolution: Set the acl attribute to private (the default). Use explicit bucket policies with specific IAM principals or aws_s3_bucket_policy resources that restrict access to known account IDs or organization units.
checks.errorMessage: S3 bucket ACL is set to authenticated-read, which grants read access to all authenticated AWS accounts worldwide, not just your organization
